text:
Jess (sales): FYI — ACME just flagged a blocker. They need per-route cost breakdowns in Console + a way to link back to traces for chargeback. Asking for CSV export and scheduled report. Wants demo by end of next month.
Sam (product): Noted. Can you paste ACME's ask and reasoning here? How many routes/endpoints do they expect to show?
Jess (sales): Quote from their TPM: 'We need chargeback to lines of business. CFO requires monthly bill by endpoint and ability to query high-cost requests.' They currently have ~120 public routes, but only ~15 high-traffic.
Nina (support): We already have 3 other tickets asking for per-route breakdown + request-level trace links (support-452, support-477, support-501).
Matt (data): We have ingestion events that include `route`, `model`, `tokens`, `latency_ms`, `customer_id`. Cardinality is fine for aggregated metrics, but request-level linking needs `request_id` persisted with trace id. Storage cost for full request logs is non-trivial.
Kai (eng): Scope question: do they want raw per-request token accounting or aggregated? Full per-request token-level billing at scale is expensive. We could do aggregated per-route token counts + top N example requests with trace links.
Sam (product): Proposal: MVP = aggregated per-route cost table (30d/90d), top 10 high-cost requests per route with link to trace, CSV export, simple API endpoint for querying per-route costs. Launch criteria: accuracy within 2% of billing, CSV export, trace links resolve for 95% of sampled requests, and security review passed.
Jess (sales): That sounds reasonable. ACME will accept aggregated if they can see sample traces for high-cost requests. Timeline: they pushed for end of next month but can be flexible if we get a clear plan.
Kai (eng): Implementation notes: we need to emit or persist the following telemetry fields on request completion: 
```
event: "inference.request.complete"
attrs: {
  request_id, route, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, duration_ms, customer_id, shard_id
}
```
We can then aggregate by route and join to traces by `request_id`.
Matt (data): Agree. We should add a daily rollup job that emits `route_cost_daily` with `route, date, tokens_total, duration_p50, tokens_cost_estimate`. That reduces query load.
Sam (product): Risk/constraints: 1) PII/Risk — ensure no plaintext user content gets into exports. 2) Storage/cost — need quotas. 3) Multi-tenant visibility: only show routes scoped to customer's org.
Nina (support): Also confirm: do we default this off for existing Hosted customers? Some orgs asked to opt-in. ACME is on Dedicated but we'd want to test on it first.
Kai (eng): Rollout plan idea: implement backend + daily rollups, enable UI feature flag. Canary on Dedicated customers (ACME), then roll to hosted with `opt-in` setting.
Sam (product): Owners: Sam -> product spec and acceptance criteria; Kai -> eng lead; Matt -> data lead; Nina -> support & docs; Jess -> customer comms.
Jess (sales): I'll get ACME to sign a short pilot agreement and share acceptance tests.
Sam (product): For prioritization: estimate 3 sprints to backend + rollups, 1 sprint UI table + CSV, 1 sprint polishing + canary. That suggests ~5 sprints (8-10 weeks). If sales wants faster, we can scope down to read-only CSV + sample traces first (2-3 weeks). Thoughts?
Kai (eng): 2-3 week quick-path would be: (1) add telemetry fields + immediate ad-hoc CSV exporter for last 30 days, (2) UI link to raw CSV only. No fancy table yet. That requires fast DB access for range queries.
Sam (product): Decision: do quick-path for ACME pilot (CSV + trace links) to meet near-term ask, while scheduling full console experience for the 5-sprint plan. I'll update intake board and create JIRA epics.
telemetry-bot: New alert: telemetry-schema-change requested by Kai. Please follow schema review checklist.
Sam (product): Action items: @Kai - open PR for telemetry + schema docs; @Matt - design rollup job and cost estimate calc; @Nina - draft support KB and export sanitization rules; @Jess - get pilot agreement + acceptance tests from ACME. I'll own the product spec doc and acceptance criteria.
Jess (sales): Thanks — I'll ping again once ACME signs pilot. :thumbsup:
Kai (eng): On it. I'll aim to have telemetry PR in 3 working days.
Matt (data): I'll mock the daily rollup output and share numbers for storage cost by EOD Friday.
Nina (support): I'll draft the KB and a checklist for export-sensitive fields.
Sam (product): Perfect. Closing the triage for now — will reopen if ACME changes scope.
